uncited: A pre-trained NeRF model representing the original scene.
A set of input images with known camera poses.
A single-view annotation (mask) identifying the object to be removed.
An updated NeRF model representing the scene with the object removed.
Inpainted images and depth maps for the input views.
*   **Guiding Images:** 2D RGB images generated by the MST inpainting network.
*   **Guiding Depth:** 2D depth maps generated by the MST inpainting network.
**Mask Generation:** Generate an initial mask for the target object using a one-shot segmentation method.
This is done from a single-view annotation.
**Loss Computation:** Compute the pixel reconstruction loss between the rendered output of the NeRF and the guiding images.
The optimization is performed over the input views.
The 2D inpainting may produce results that are inconsistent across different viewpoints, leading to artifacts in the 3D reconstruction.
This can lead to suboptimal results if the inpainted regions are unreliable in certain views.
Uses SAM for segmentation and propagates edits via depth consistency rather than relying on a separate 2D inpainting network for guidance.
Choose when geometric consistency is prioritized over texture synthesis fidelity. [Link](13674-local-editing-via-sam-and-depth-propagation.md)
*   **Time Complexity:** Depends on the optimization steps for the NeRF and the inference time of the MST inpainting network.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Standard NeRF memory requirements plus storage for guiding images and depth maps.
*   **When to use:** When high-quality 2D inpainting is available and 3D consistency is secondary or can be tolerated.
